items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Francis Murray, who you probably don't remember, he was a young man, and a saxophone player where he used to play stories about Joe Clancy.

ctx.x: Most musicians, Dick, would actually use, most of the good players would use two and a half to three. Some extremists would use four, real hard reeds, but most of the guys would play a two and a half to three. And, to get the right sound, most of them used a medium open lay mouthpiece. Again, some of the guys would use. It depended on how, depended on how, how they wanted to sound. You know, mouthpiece is really, if you have your choice between a good horn and a bad mouthpiece and a good mouthpiece and a bad…

Well Joe Clancy is famous, the stories about him. Yeah. Francis Murray, who you probably don't remember, he was a young man, and a saxophone player where he used to play stories about Joe Clancy. Well anyway, was there any special sort of ligature you used to, or that people generally use since you worked in the store?

Ligatures, most all of them are made in France, and there are different names put on them. The banal, the O-N-A-B-E, is what I actually used. But there are so many different variations of them. I just recently sent one that I got to put Brown in the water. And, Bud, I knew in St. Louis, his brother lives here in town.
